articles.title: Touchline ban reduced for Rangers manager McInnes
articles.summary: Rangers manager Derek McInnes has a touchline ban reduced to two games, with two suspended, following an appeal against the original penalty for comments made on a last-gasp Celtic penalty.
body: The 55-year-old will be in the stands for Wednesday's visit to Falkirk and Saturday's home match against Motherwell.
He will return to the dugout for the rescheduled visit of St Mirren to Ibrox on 9 September.

The original penalty of a four-match touchline ban, with one suspended, was issued in July and related to McInnes' spell as Hearts boss last season, when he described the decision to award Celtic a late penalty at Motherwell in May as "disgusting", adding "we are up against everybody".

The stoppage-time spot-kick for handball was converted by Kelechi Iheanacho and Celtic's 3-2 victory at Fir Park on 13 May kept them one point behind Hearts, who they beat to the title three days later in a final-day decider.

articles.title: Who would fall in love with a fake NFL player? Plenty of sensible people
articles.summary: The FBI has charged Daejon Love after he allegedly pretended to be a 49ers receiver. Although football isn’t as glamorous as it looks, it easy to see the attraction. Is romance dead? Yeah, probably.
body: I s romance dead? Yeah, probably. There have never been more options for finding a mate – dating apps, Instagram DM slides, hanging out next to a gas station at 2am – but it’s also never been harder. Meeting someone who is compatible, stable, and even remotely attractive is akin to putting a square peg in a round hole. Blindfolded. From a mile away. Underwater. So, I can’t blame anyone for falling for an elaborate hoax like the one allegedly perpetrated by Daejon Love.

The FBI claims Love enticed women into romantic correspondence, then asked them for money to place into “lucrative investments.” In one of many videos obtained by TMZ, Love states he was looking for “ genetically superior women.” Then again, aren’t we all?

articles.title: Liverpool sign Barcola in £123m deal and expect Gakpo to stay after City offer £80m
articles.summary: France international says title ‘one of my biggest dreams’ Club rejected weekend Gakpo bid from Manchester City. Bradley Barcola is aiming to win the Premier League after completing his move to Liverpool from Paris Saint-Germain for an initial £106m, which could rise to £123m.
body: Andoni Iraola has prioritised signing wingers this summer after replacing Arne Slot. Barcola follows the arrival of Victor Muñoz as the former Bournemouth head coach aims to rebuild the front line.

“It took a long time but I’m really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play,” Barcola said. “I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it’s one of my biggest dreams in my life. It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that’s why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.”

Barcola, who will be 24 on Wednesday, was a long-term target for Liverpool, who have tracked his progress over a number of seasons. Completing the transfer has been delayed while PSG waited to make signings to compensate for the exit of the former Lyon player, who attracted interested from other clubs but was adamant that he was willing only to join Liverpool.

articles.title: Goals, records, tears ... Messi's most iconic moments
articles.summary: As Lionel Messi retires from international football following the death of his father, BBC Sport looks back at some of his most iconic moments.
body: The 39-year-old, who is signed with Inter Miami until 2028, announced on Monday his successful time with Argentina had come to an end after more than 20 years.
Messi said he was considering his future in football following the death of his father, Jorge, earlier this month.

In an emotional tribute to his dad, he hinted at retirement as he said: "I don't know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I'm really not sure if I'll carry on doing it for much longer."

And now he has made public his decision to call time on his international career in a post on Instagram, external, saying: "Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply."

articles.title: Pakistan drop seven players and release head coach
articles.summary: Pakistan respond to their series defeat by England by taking the extraordinary step of dropping seven players, calling up five uncapped players and releasing their head coach.
body: After two one-sided defeats in the first two Tests, the tourists have revamped their squad and backroom staff for the third and final match of the series at Edgbaston.

Five of the players dropped - Muhammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman and Khurram Shahzad - have featured in the series so far, while Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Jafar have been sent home without playing.
A total of seven players have been called up. Batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have previous Test experience and join the quintet of uncapped newcomers.
Spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas, left-arm seamer Mohammed Imran Jr, wicketkeeper Said Baig and all-rounders Mohammad Imran and Razaullah have all received call-ups.

articles.title: ‘She is dominating the sport’: Dave Portnoy says Caitlin Clark is WNBA MVP
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark’s WNBA MVP odds are still lagging behind a couple of other stars, but Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy doesn’t think the race should be close at all. Currently, Clark has the fourth-best odds (+5000) on DraftKings to take home the league’s biggest individual honor.
body: On “Wake Up Barstool” Monday, Portnoy made his case that Clark is the clear-cut MVP, arguing that she is ‘dominating the sport’ the way people anticipated she would when the came to the WNBA in 2024.
Portnoy is an unabashed Clark supporter, but insisted his bias isn’t why the third-year guard should win her first MVP trophy.

“Caitlin Clark is the MVP, and I’m not just saying it because I’m a Caitlin Clark fan,” Portnoy began. “The numbers, and what she has been doing for the last month. The last game, 34 points, 12 assists. Game before that, 37 points, 10 assists…In her last 10 games: 34, 37, 21, 24, 26, 29, 22 (points). She’s a double-double machine. The league has never seen anything like it.”
As for critics who tried to claim Clark was “overrated” and “can’t shoot,” Portnoy noted that Clark’s three-point shooting is “coming around” and is up to 37.3% on the season.

articles.title: Is Lionel Messi retiring from Inter Miami too? Argentina decision raises fresh questions over his future
articles.summary: Lionel Messi’s Argentina retirement has put a question mark over the rest of his career. The 39-year-old is not calling time on football just yet, but the end is clearly approaching. The news broke on Monday, with Messi announcing his international retirement in an emotional Instagram post.
body: Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami through the end of the 2028 season. He has not given any indication he is walking away early.

The Athletic’s reports suggest an end to his club career could be near, though. Few players are as tied to their national team as Messi, and without a World Cup or Copa America to aim for, the motivation could fade.

His numbers in Miami, though, show he is still producing at an elite level. Messi has 98 goals and 54 assists in 111 games for the club, an average of 1.36 goal involvements per match. That is better than his Argentina record, which sits at 0.89 per game.
Age is clearly not a problem in Major League Soccer. But the bigger question is what drives him now that international football is gone.

articles.title: Is now the right time for Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' US Open loss?
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic said he "despised" every moment of the five-set, near five-hour ordeal which ended his US Open hopes in the first round, so now the question is whether he calls time on his trophy-laden career.
body: The 24-time Grand Slam champion was knocked out in the first round of the US Open for the first time, beaten by Mariano Navone of Argentina.
Djokovic was 19-0 in the US Open first round and hadn't lost his opening match in any major since Paul Goldstein beat him at the Australian Open in 2006.
The 39-year-old also admitted the underlying health issue he first revealed two weeks ago was "serious", although he remains intent on getting the problem fixed.

Djokovic looked physically spent, was repeatedly sick and regularly doubled over in pain. He held back tears at one point but managed a gracious smile as he congratulated world No 49 Navone on the biggest win of his career.

articles.title: Constitution Hill set for serious test at Kempton on Saturday
articles.summary: Constitution Hill looks likely to face a serious examination of his big-race ambitions on the Flat when he goes for the William Hill September Stakes at Kempton Park on Saturday, with new jockey Billy Loughnane in the saddle.
body: Nicky Henderson's former superstar hurdler is two from two since switching to the level, but the Group Three contest at the Sunbury track represents a major step up.

The nine-year-old has been ridden by Oisin Murphy and Ryan Moore so far in his new adventure, but Loughnane's name appeared alongside the Seven Barrows runner for the weekend on the British Horseracing Authority administration site.
Loughnane's agent Tony Hind, who also represents Moore, confirmed the switch saying that Henderson was happy for the championship-leading jockey to take over on Michael Buckley's pride and joy.

"His first choice was Ryan who is riding in America," he said. "So I offered him Billy who is definitely there riding in the Sirenia Stakes and Nicky confirmed this morning he was fine for Billy to ride."

articles.title: Pakistan drop seven players from Test squad after England series defeat
articles.summary: Pakistan have dropped seven players and two coaches from their touring squad following their series defeat to England and ahead of the final Test at Edgbaston.
body: Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq - injured during the second Test defeat at Lord's - Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad have all been sent home.
Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul have also been released and will be replaced by Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke in the backroom staff.
Seven replacements have been called up to the squad, including five uncapped players at Test level, with batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal having eight and two Test appearances, respectively.

Left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas has represented Pakistan in white-ball cricket, with left-arm fast bowler Mohammad Imran Jnr, wicketkeeper-batter Saad Baig and pace-bowling all-rounders Mohammad Imran (also known as Imran Randhawa) and Razaullah the others brought in.
